name: Eye whitening and brightening

card.summary: Efforts to make the whites of the eyes look whiter and brighter, discussed for contrast and a fresher look; little research targets this goal.
card.aka: White sclera, bright eyes, redness-reducing drops
card.note: Eye drops marketed for redness are a medical product category; users report trying them, and no study reviewed here tests them for appearance.

quick.overview:
Eye whitening and brightening refers to making the sclera (the white of the eye) look whiter and less red so the eyes appear fresher and higher in contrast. Users on looksmax.org describe white sclera and bright eyes as important for every eye colour because of contrast.

The sources found for this entry are thin. Published research reviewed is not about cosmetic eye whitening, so the article is short.
quick.mechanism: Proponents talk about reducing redness and the contrast between iris and sclera, and mention using eye drops. No studies reviewed examine how such methods affect perceived attractiveness.
quick.risks: Wikipedia's eye drop article does not cover redness-relieving drops in depth; it says alpha agonist drops used for glaucoma have a higher likelihood of allergic reaction and list burning, stinging and other side effects. Persistent redness is commonly a reason for medical review.

lead: Eye whitening and brightening covers the ways people try to make the sclera, the white of the eye, look whiter and less red so the eyes appear clearer, more contrasted and fresher. Looksmaxxing users describe it as a quick contrast adjustment: a whiter sclera makes the iris look more saturated and the area around the eyes look cleaner.[1][2]

The methods discussed in forums are mostly everyday ones. One looksmax.org poster lists a redness-relieving drop (Lumify) as his quickest option, with sleep, hydration and screen breaks as longer-term contributors, and pairs sclera brightness with whiter teeth as a contrast pair.[1] Another poster says sclera whiteness matters for every eye colour and especially for brown eyes, and mentions eye drops.[2] Lumify is a brand of brimonidine, an alpha-2 agonist that is also used in glaucoma drops and a rosacea gel.[4]

Scientific work on the white sclera concerns its role in human gaze signalling and social perception rather than cosmetic whitening: researchers have studied why humans have a uniformly white sclera and how children respond to faces with white versus dark sclera.[5][6] No study has tested cosmetic eye whitening for attractiveness.

paras: The sclera is the white outer layer of the eye. Looksmaxxing posts describe a dull, grey or red sclera as reducing the contrast of the eye area, and a white, clear sclera as making the iris look more saturated and the gaze more energetic.[1] Some posters also say it can help a face look good in photos, and that bright eyes matter more for people with brown eyes.[2]

In one looksmax.org thread the original poster names a brimonidine-based redness drop as the easiest option and says eyes look clearer in the minutes after applying it; he also lists sleep, hydration, regular blinking and breaks from screens as contributors to a brighter sclera.[1] Another poster says he uses eye drops and asks for other suggestions; replies discuss eyeliner or makeup at the lateral canthus and its effect on perceived eye shape.[2]

Brimonidine is an alpha-2 adrenergic agonist: as drops it lowers pressure in open-angle glaucoma, as a gel it treats facial redness in rosacea, and it is also used to reduce redness of the eye. Wikipedia lists itchiness, redness and dry mouth among common eye-drop side effects, and allergic reaction among more serious ones.[4] The general eye-drop article notes that drops carry a lower risk of side effects than oral medicines and that redness lasting more than three days on lubricant drops is a reason to seek medical advice.[3]

Researchers in cognitive science propose that the exposed, uniformly white human sclera evolved to make eye-gaze easier for others to read, and a 2023 review in Trends in Cognitive Sciences updates that hypothesis.[5] A separate 2023 paper reported white sclera in chimpanzees and other mammals, and a 2022 study examined how conspicuous chimpanzee gaze is at realistic distances.[7][8] In a 2023 study, five-year-old children rated faces with white sclera as more cooperative than faces with dark sclera.[6] These studies address eye morphology and social perception, not cosmetic whitening.
No studies found of eye whitening or brightening for appearance. Related research on the evolution and social perception of the white sclera is described above.[5][6]

lore.intro: The topic appears in looksmax.org threads about eye contrast, where sclera whiteness is paired with other contrast features such as teeth.[1][2]

claims.claim: White sclera and bright eyes improve eye appearance through contrast.
claims.believers: Posters say a clear sclera makes the iris look more saturated and the face look cleaner, and that it matters for every eye colour, especially brown.[1][2] One reply argued that teeth matter more, and that with hooded eyes or a strong brow ridge the eye area is dark enough that sclera changes are barely visible.[1]
claims.experts: No published study has tested whether sclera whiteness affects perceived attractiveness; research on white sclera concerns gaze signalling and cooperation judgements.[5][6]

claims.claim: Redness-relieving drops give a quick brightening effect.
claims.believers: A poster calls a brimonidine-based drop his easiest option, saying eyes look clearer within one to two minutes of applying it.[1]
claims.experts: Brimonidine is documented as an alpha-2 agonist used in eye drops and rosacea gel, with itching, redness and dry mouth listed among common side effects.[4] No study reviewed tests it as an appearance enhancer.

claims.claim: Sleep, hydration and fewer screen hours produce a whiter sclera over time.
claims.believers: The same poster says dryness and fatigue make the sclera look grey or red, and that sleep, water and screen breaks are the real long-term contributors.[1]
claims.experts: No studies reviewed examine these habits in relation to sclera colour for cosmetic purposes.

angle.text: Users aim to make the whites of the eyes look clearer, which they say increases contrast with the iris and makes the eye area look more awake. They talk about redness-relieving drops for a short-term effect and sleep, hydration and screen breaks for longer-term clarity.
